reports.title: UK Electricity Mix Weekly Report: Saturday 26 September
reports.intro: A measured weekly report for EnergyMix.info using the available 7-day historical generation feed for Sunday 20 September to Friday 25 September.
reports.summary: The week from Sunday 20 September to Friday 25 September averaged about 25.8 GW of measured generation, with renewables averaging 39.3% of measured output. The strongest renewable day in the available data was Sunday 20 September, when wind, solar and hydro together averaged 60.7% of measured generation. Gas was highest on Tuesday 22 September and lowest on Sunday 20 September.
reports.takeaway: For flexible electricity use, the cleanest opportunities are likely to appear when wind is strong, gas is low and demand is not at a peak. This is the foundation for future EV-charging guidance, clean-electricity alerts and weekly newsletter summaries.
drivers: Renewables were strongest on Sunday 20 September, when wind, solar and hydro averaged 60.7% of measured generation.
Wind was the largest swing factor in the available feed, peaking at about 11.4 GW average output on Sunday 20 September.
Solar was strongest on Sunday 20 September, averaging about 3.6 GW across settlement periods after embedded-solar backfill where needed.
Gas averaged about 8.4 GW across the period, rising highest on Tuesday 22 September and falling lowest on Sunday 20 September.
Measured generation was highest on Wednesday 23 September, at roughly 26.8 GW average output.

cleanestPeriods.title: Best low-carbon proxy: Sunday 20 September
cleanestPeriods.body: Historical carbon-intensity aggregates are not yet part of this weekly report feed, so EnergyMix.info uses renewable share and gas output as cautious proxies. Sunday 20 September had the strongest renewable share at 60.7%.

cleanestPeriods.title: Lowest gas proxy: Sunday 20 September
cleanestPeriods.body: Gas generation averaged about 4.5 GW on Sunday 20 September. Lower gas periods are often cleaner, but the report does not yet claim this was the lowest-carbon period without historical carbon-intensity validation.

higherCarbonPeriods.title: Highest gas proxy: Tuesday 22 September
higherCarbonPeriods.body: Gas averaged about 12.2 GW on Tuesday 22 September. Gas-heavy periods are usually higher-carbon, but this is labelled as a proxy until historical carbon-intensity highs/lows are added to the report feed.

socialPosts.title: Monday weekly grid brief
socialPosts.body:
Last week in Britain’s electricity mix:

• Highest renewable share in the available feed: 60.7% on Sunday 20 September
• Highest average wind output: ~11.4 GW on Sunday 20 September
• Highest average solar output: ~3.6 GW on Sunday 20 September
• Highest average gas output: ~12.2 GW on Tuesday 22 September

The shift was clear: gas-heavy weekdays gave way to a cleaner, wind-led weekend.

Full report: https://energymix.info/reports/weekly/2026-09-26/

socialPosts.title: Wednesday explainer
socialPosts.body:
What does “UK electricity mix” actually mean?

For live grid dashboards, it usually means Great Britain’s electricity system: England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is part of the UK, but operates in a separate electricity market.

Explainer: https://energymix.info/uk-electricity-mix

socialPosts.title: Friday practical clean-electricity post
socialPosts.body:
The cleanest time to use electricity is not a fixed hour.

It changes with wind, solar, demand, imports and gas generation. Windy overnight periods and sunny middays can be much cleaner than still early-evening peaks.

Guide: https://energymix.info/cleanest-time-to-use-electricity
